# Intake Brief: Divide the competitive score target by the number of players

**Work item:** MS-0MUZH6V7C0091SGE · `feature` · `critical`
**Seed intent (operator):** "The target score for a game should be divided by the number of players."
**Supersedes:** MS-0MUUE0FVZ001VE2D (Competitive mode: halve the score target per AI opponent) — producer decision 2026-10-08, Q1 = (a).

## Headline

In competitive (human vs AI) games the win target is currently the full single-player
`config.winThreshold` (Easy 10000 / Medium 12000 / Hard 15000), so a game against more
opponents does not get any shorter per seat. This item makes the effective target the base
threshold **divided by the number of players** (`playerCount`, human + AI) and **rounded to
the nearest 50**, and makes every engine and player-facing use of the target agree on that one
derived value.

## Problem statement

Competitive mode uses a single shared `config.winThreshold` for the first-to-threshold win
check, the AI look-ahead and every player-facing score readout. The operator wants the target
score to scale down with the number of players so a larger roster still reaches the win
condition in a comparable run length. Today no such scaling exists anywhere.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the "x / y" target shown in the HUD, score tooltip and help panel to match
  the value the engine actually awards a win at, and to be achievable in a sensible number of
  turns regardless of how many AI seats are in the game.
- **Balance designer / producer** — wants one authoritative, testable formula for the
  competitive target so future balancing levers are unambiguous.
- **Developer** — wants a single source of truth (helper) rather than the same arithmetic
  duplicated across engine, AI and UI.

User story: *As a player starting a competitive game against two AI opponents, I want the score
target divided by the number of players so the race stays winnable in a comparable run length
to single-player.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Effective target formula.** In a competitive game with `P` players (`state.playerCount`, human + AI) the win check threshold equals `roundToNearest50(baseWinThreshold / P)` — `Math.round(baseWinThreshold / P / 50) * 50` — and the first seat whose per-owner score reaches it is declared `competitiveWinnerId`.
- **AC2 — Consistent everywhere.** The HUD `Score: x / y` line, the score tooltip (`x / y`, "remaining to win") and the help panel "Reach N points to win" text all show the effective competitive threshold, never the base value.
- **AC3 — Single-player unchanged.** Single-player (no `players[]` / `playerCount` undefined) continues to use the base `winThreshold`, which is already a multiple of 50 so the rounding is a no-op.
- **AC4 — AI parity.** The AI look-ahead `aiPlanningHorizon` and the per-seat `aiCompetitivePlanningHorizon` use the effective win threshold, so the AI plans toward the win condition it is racing toward.
- **AC5 — Save/load round-trip.** A resumed competitive game re-derives the effective win threshold from the persisted `playerCount`; no stale threshold survives a load.
- **AC6 — Testing and validation.** New Vitest coverage for AC1–AC5 (engine, AI, UI strings, serialisation) and the full project test suite passes; the new tests fail against the pre-change code.
- **AC7 — Documentation.** The competitive win-condition description in `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` states the `base / playerCount`, rounded to the nearest 50, effective win threshold rule, and touched code comments are updated.

*Metric:* each AC is pass/fail via the tests named in its child slices — see the plan decomposition.
## Constraints

- **Single-player must not change.** Division by one player is the only single-player effect;
  no behaviour shift there.
- **Do not change base difficulty presets** (Easy/Medium/Hard `winThreshold` values in
  `src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts`) — derive the effective value at consumption time.
- **Do not change** challenge-complete instant win, bankruptcy, reputation-collapse,
  last-standing, or endless-mode continuation semantics (MS-0MTIILU5V006GCN4).
- **One source of truth.** Introduce a single pure helper for the effective threshold and use it
  at every engine/AI/UI site; do not duplicate the arithmetic.
- **UK English** in all comments, docs and UI copy.
- No `CHANGELOG.md` edits (managed by the ship/release pipeline).

## Existing state

- `config.winThreshold` is a single shared value (Easy 10000, Medium 12000, Hard 15000) in
  `src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts`.
- Competitive win check compares each `PlayerRecord.score` to `config.winThreshold`
  (`checkCompetitiveEndConditions`, `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts:1058`), including the
  endless-mode branch (`endReason = 'score_threshold_continue'`).
- AI look-ahead reads `config.winThreshold` directly
  (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts:134` in `aiPlanningHorizon`, and `:1821` in
  `aiCompetitivePlanningHorizon`).
- Player-facing displays read `config.winThreshold`:
  `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts:221` (HUD `Score: x / y`),
  `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts:290` (score tooltip),
  `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts:128` (help "Reach N points to win", fed from
  `buildMainStreetHelpContent(s.state.config)` in `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts:365`).
- `playerCount` is set by `createCompetitiveState` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts:586`) and is
  already serialised/restored (`src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts:93`, `:649`).
- Competitive rosters are bounded: `MIN_AI_OPPONENTS = 1`, `MAX_AI_OPPONENTS = 3`
  (`src/scenes/MainStreetNewGameSelection.ts:32-33`), so `P ∈ {2, 3, 4}`.
- No `effectiveWinThreshold` / effective-target helper exists today (grep confirmed).

## Desired change

Add a pure helper in `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` (re-exported via `src/MainStreetState.ts`
if needed):

```ts
/**
 * Effective win threshold. Competitive games divide the difficulty base
 * threshold by the number of seats (human + AI), rounded to the nearest 50
 * so the target stays a round, displayable number. Single-player has no
 * `playerCount`, so it resolves to the base threshold unchanged.
 */
export function effectiveWinThreshold(state: MainStreetState): number {
  const players = state.playerCount ?? 1;
  return Math.round(state.config.winThreshold / players / 50) * 50;
}
```

Route every win-check, AI-horizon and player-facing display site through it. Single-player
resolves to the base value because `playerCount` is undefined. Because `playerCount` is already
persisted, save/load needs no new field — only a test asserting the re-derived value.

Worked values (base → effective):

| Base (preset) | P=2 | P=3 | P=4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Easy 10000 | 5000 | 3350 | 2500 |
| Medium 12000 | 6000 | 4000 | 3000 |
| Hard 15000 | 7500 | 5000 | 3750 |

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` — home for the new pure `effectiveWinThreshold(state)` helper
  (alongside `computeScore`), re-exported via `src/MainStreetState.ts` if needed.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — use the helper in `checkCompetitiveEndConditions`
  (single-player path stays `checkEndConditions`), including the endless-mode branch.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `aiPlanningHorizon` and `aiCompetitivePlanningHorizon` use the
  helper instead of `config.winThreshold`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — HUD `Score: x / y` denominator.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — `buildScoreTooltip` threshold/remaining lines.
- `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` — help panel "Reach N points to win" receives the effective
  threshold from state; caller `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` passes it.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — read-only reference; `playerCount` already persisted.
- `src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — read-only reference; base presets must not change.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-end-condition-ai-win.test.ts` — extend the competitive win-check
  coverage for P = 2..4.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts` — extend the AI horizon coverage.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-hud.test.ts` — HUD `Score: x / y` string.
- `tests/main-street/hud-tooltips.test.ts` — score tooltip `x / y` and "remaining to win".
- `tests/main-street/help-panel-content.test.ts` — help "Reach N points to win" string.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-save-load.test.ts` — re-derived threshold after load.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — Section 7 win-condition rule.

## Plan decomposition

Four test-first vertical slices (each writes failing tests first, then implementation, then a
green suite):

1. **Effective threshold helper and competitive win check** — MS-0MUZK64F8000XYO0 *(high;
   prerequisite for 2–4)* — the pure helper, the standard and endless competitive win check,
   single-player parity, and the save/load regression guards. *(AC1, AC3, AC5)*
2. **AI look-ahead uses the effective win threshold** — MS-0MUZK64R5008Z8MA *(depends on 1)* —
   both planning-horizon helpers. *(AC4)*
3. **Player-facing win target consistency HUD tooltip help** — MS-0MUZK652V001L71C *(depends on
   1)* — HUD, score tooltip and help panel. *(AC2)*
4. **Document the competitive target rule and validate the suite** — MS-0MUZK65EI004X4UB
   *(depends on 1)* — the Section 7 docs rule and the documented-value sweep. *(AC7)*

AC6 (new tests fail pre-change; full `npm test` green) is verified inside every slice. The
persistence assertions in slice 1 are regression guards (they are green once the helper lands,
but fail if the `?? 1` default is removed or a derived threshold is persisted).

## Related work

- **MS-0MUUE0FVZ001VE2D** — Competitive mode: halve the score target per AI opponent.
  **Superseded by this item** (producer decision 2026-10-08, Q1 = a). Its `base × 0.5^N`
  formula agrees with `base / P` only at two players; it is closed, not implemented.
- **MS-0MUXLGCQC000W7ZE** — Add test cases for AI and human win threshold in competitive mode
  (open) — test precedent for competitive threshold behaviour.
- **MS-0MUXLP6V00075IQY** — Fix win/loss attribution in `checkCompetitiveEndConditions`
  (blocked) — touches the same function; slice 1 should be rebased on it if it lands first.
- **MS-0MUR9IMXE0090WIV** — Confirm win thresholds / run length as the difficulty lever (open) —
  balance context for run length.
- **MS-0MT5X3GMA007EG30** — Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street
  (completed) — origin of the shared first-to-threshold rule.
- **MS-0MTIILU5V006GCN4** — Competitive endless continuation beyond win threshold (completed) —
  endless-mode branch must use the effective threshold without changing semantics.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

- **MS-0MTIILU5V006GCN4** – Competitive endless continuation (beyond win threshold) (completed)
- **MS-0MUYFXA36009EMH0** – Per-seat animated competitive closing (completed)
- **MS-0MUTU8INS009MRR1** – Game-mode selector UI (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: competitive, discovered, game, intent, mode, number, operator, players, score, seed, should, target
- `docs/main-street/balance-guardrail-recommendations.md` — matched: competitive, game, intent, mode, number, operator, opponent, players, score, seed, should, target
- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: game, intent, mode, number, operator, opponent, players, score, seed, should, target

> The keyword matches above are low-precision (shared vocabulary); the manual **Related work** list is the authoritative set. Full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-MS-0MUZH6V7C0091SGE.md`.

## Assumptions

- **"Number of players" = total seats, including the human** (i.e. `state.playerCount`), not
  "number of AI opponents". Confirmed by the producer decision on Q1 (2026-10-08).
- **Rounding:** the quotient is rounded to the **nearest 50** (`Math.round(base / P / 50) * 50`),
  so Easy/P=3 → 3350 rather than 3333. Ties round up (`Math.round` semantics). Confirmed by the
  producer decision on Q2 (2026-10-08).
- **Competitive-only effect:** single-player has one player, so division by one leaves the base
  value unchanged by construction.
- The operator's `base / P` formula is the current intent and **supersedes** the compounding
  `0.5^N` formula recorded on MS-0MUUE0FVZ001VE2D; that item is closed as superseded.

## Risks

- **Engine/UI divergence** — if any display site keeps reading `config.winThreshold` the player
  sees a target the engine does not use. *Mitigation:* single helper + a grep/test sweep for
  remaining win-threshold decision sites (exclude single-player/legacy paths deliberately).
- **Legacy saves** missing `playerCount` must default to divisor 1, not break. *Mitigation:*
  `?? 1` default plus a load test.
- **Balance drift** — a lower target shortens competitive runs, possibly interacting with the
  run-length lever. *Mitigation:* flag to MS-0MUR9IMXE0090WIV; keep the change a single derived
  formula so it is trivially reversible.
- **Scope creep** into single-player or difficulty presets. *Mitigation:* Constraints above;
  log any follow-on as separate work.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q0 (seed intent).** What is the requested behaviour? — **Answer (operator):** "The target
  score for a game should be divided by the number of players." Source: `/intake` invocation,
  2026-10-08. Priority `critical` supplied by the operator.
- **Q1 (duplicate / formula conflict).** Does this item supersede the producer-confirmed formula
  on MS-0MUUE0FVZ001VE2D (`base × 0.5^N`, N = AI opponents), or should both be reconciled?
  Options were: (a) adopt `base / P` and supersede MS-0MUUE0FVZ001VE2D; (b) adopt `base × 0.5^N`
  and rewrite this item; (c) defer and reconcile later. — **Answer (operator, 2026-10-08):** (a).
  Agent recommendation was (a). MS-0MUUE0FVZ001VE2D is recorded as superseded by
  MS-0MUZH6V7C0091SGE and closed. Evidence: this work item's plan session, 2026-10-08.
- **Q2 (rounding).** For non-integer quotients (e.g. Easy 10000 ÷ 3), how should the effective
  target round? Options were: `Math.round` → 3333; `Math.ceil` → 3334; `Math.floor` → 3333. —
  **Answer (operator, 2026-10-08):** "round to the nearest 50", i.e. 3333 → **3350**. Final:
  `Math.round(base / P / 50) * 50` with ties rounding up. Agent recommendation had been
  `Math.round` (nearest integer); the operator chose the stronger nearest-50 rule, which
  supersedes that recommendation. Evidence: this work item's plan session, 2026-10-08.

**Open questions: none.** Both intake questions are resolved.

# Restructure the documentation: separate development docs from gameplay docs

**Discovered from:** `MS-0MUNB54KU005084C` (rendering the storyline graph surfaced
that `docs/main-street/` mixes audience-facing gameplay documentation with
engineering/process documentation).

## Problem statement

`docs/main-street/` is a single flat directory that mixes two very different
audiences and lifecycles:

- **Gameplay / player-facing reference** — `storylines.md`,
  `content-design-and-progression.md`, `core-rules-and-mechanics.md`,
  `card-catalog.md`, `card-dimensions.md`, `specialization-skills.md`,
  `ux-visual-audio.md`, `tutorial-localization.md`, `playtest-scenarios.md`,
  `the-build-gdd.md`.
- **Development / engineering & evidence** — `balancing-methodology.md`,
  `balance-analysis-api.md`, `balance-guardrail-recommendations.md`,
  `further-balancing-recommendations.md`, `monte-carlo-*`, `*evidence.md`,
  `prd-*.md`, `ai-strategy.md`, `analysis/`, `screenshots/`, generated
  artefacts (`storyline-graph.mmd`, `storyline-manifest.json`,
  `expanded-card-manifest.json`, `card-catalog-baseline.json`).

A reader looking for gameplay rules has to wade through balance experiments,
PRDs and evidence bundles; an engineer looking for process docs has to filter
out player-facing prose. Links between the two trees are also fragile
(relative paths, `example-games/` staleness — see `MS-0MUNC8AOL0092BE5`).

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the documentation split by audience — gameplay docs
separate from development docs — with stable, cross-linked structure, so each
audience can find what it needs and the docs build/guards stay green.

## Proposed shape (to be confirmed in intake/plan)

- `docs/game/` (or `docs/players/`) — gameplay-rule and content reference.
- `docs/dev/` — engineering, balance methodology, PRDs, evidence, process.
- Generated artefacts under a single `assets/` (or `generated/`) location.
- Cross-links updated; doc-drift guards and path-based tests updated.

## Acceptance Criteria (provisional — to be finalised by intake/plan)

1. **Audience split** — gameplay docs and development docs live in separate,
   documented trees; the split is stated in a top-level docs index.
2. **No broken links** — every relative markdown link in the moved docs
   resolves; the existing docs-path guards are updated and green.
3. **Generated artefacts** — generated files (`.mmd`, manifests, SVGs) are in a
   single, consistently referenced location.
4. **Index & navigation** — a `docs/README.md` (or equivalent) indexes both
   trees and explains the distinction.
5. **Guards & tests updated** — every test/guard that references doc paths is
   updated; the full suite passes.

## Constraints

- Do not change the documentation *content* beyond moving/linking; this is a
  structural refactor.
- Coordinate with `MS-0MUNC8AOL0092BE5` (stale `example-games/` doc paths) and
  `MS-0MUNB54KU005084C` (storyline graph docs), which touch the same tree.
- Keep changes reviewable; large moves may be decomposed during planning.

## Related work

- `MS-0MUNB54KU005084C` — storyline graph rendering/docs (discovered-from).
- `MS-0MUNC8AOL0092BE5` — fix stale `example-games/main-street` doc paths.
- `MS-0MUYK064P0032374` — static docs site (deferred).

# Slice 1: Effective-threshold helper and competitive win check

**Parent:** MS-0MUZH6V7C0091SGE (Competitive mode: divide the score target by the number of players) · slice 1 of 4
**Test-first:** write the failing Vitest cases below **before** adding the helper.

## Goal

Introduce the single source of truth for the competitive win target and make the competitive
win check use it, so a game with `P` seats (human + AI) is won at
`Math.round(baseWinThreshold / P / 50) * 50`.

Worked values (base → effective): Easy 10000 → P=2 5000, P=3 3350, P=4 2500;
Medium 12000 → 6000 / 4000 / 3000; Hard 15000 → 7500 / 5000 / 3750.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (parent AC1).** In a competitive game with `P` players (`state.playerCount`, human + AI) the win check threshold equals `roundToNearest50(baseWinThreshold / P)` — `Math.round(baseWinThreshold / P / 50) * 50` — and the first seat whose per-owner score reaches it is declared `competitiveWinnerId`. Slice tests pin Easy P=2 5000, P=3 3350, P=4 2500 and are written red before the helper exists.
- **AC2 (parent AC1).** In a competitive game with `P` players (`state.playerCount`, human + AI) the win check threshold equals `roundToNearest50(baseWinThreshold / P)` — `Math.round(baseWinThreshold / P / 50) * 50` — and the first seat whose per-owner score reaches it is declared `competitiveWinnerId`. A single pure `effectiveWinThreshold(state)` returns `Math.round(state.config.winThreshold / (state.playerCount ?? 1) / 50) * 50`, and no other site in `src/` duplicates the division.
- **AC3 (parent AC1).** In a competitive game with `P` players (`state.playerCount`, human + AI) the win check threshold equals `roundToNearest50(baseWinThreshold / P)` — `Math.round(baseWinThreshold / P / 50) * 50` — and the first seat whose per-owner score reaches it is declared `competitiveWinnerId`. The competitive win check compares each per-owner score against the effective win threshold for P = 2, 3, 4 and declares that seat `competitiveWinnerId` with `endReason = 'score_threshold'`.
- **AC4 (parent AC3).** Single-player (no `players[]` / `playerCount` undefined) continues to use the base `winThreshold`, which is already a multiple of 50 so the rounding is a no-op. The competitive entry point delegates to `checkEndConditions` and an explicit assertion pins the unchanged base value.
- **AC5 (parent AC5).** A resumed competitive game re-derives the effective win threshold from the persisted `playerCount`; no stale threshold survives a load. A serialise then deserialise round-trip of a P=3 Easy state re-derives 3350; a legacy save with no `playerCount` yields the base threshold.
- **AC6 (parent AC6).** New Vitest coverage for AC1–AC5 (engine, AI, UI strings, serialisation) and the full project test suite passes; the new tests fail against the pre-change code. (this slice: helper, competitive win check, persistence guards).
- **AC7.** The endless-mode branch uses the effective win threshold and keeps `endReason = 'score_threshold_continue'` and its idempotent re-entry behaviour unchanged.

*Metric:* unit tests for AC1–AC4 red then green; source grep for AC2; regression-guard test for AC5; `npm test` for AC6 and AC7.
## Minimal implementation

- Add `effectiveWinThreshold(state)` to `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` with a doc comment
  stating the competitive `base / playerCount`, nearest-50 rule and the single-player no-op.
- Re-export it from `src/MainStreetState.ts` if consumers import through the barrel.
- Replace `state.config.winThreshold` with the helper in `checkCompetitiveEndConditions`
  (both the standard and endless branches) in `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`; leave
  `checkEndConditions` untouched.
- Add the round-trip and legacy-save guards to the competitive save/load suite.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`
- `src/MainStreetState.ts`
- `tests/main-street/competitive-end-condition-ai-win.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/competitive-save-load.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- None. This slice is the prerequisite for slices 2–4.
- Note: MS-0MUXLP6V00075IQY (Fix win/loss attribution in `checkCompetitiveEndConditions`,
  blocked) touches the same function — rebase on it if it lands first.

## Deliverables

- `effectiveWinThreshold` helper with unit coverage.
- Competitive win check (standard + endless) routed through the helper.
- Persistence regression guards.

data.description:
# Ask about the tutorial before the single-player/competitive choice

## Problem statement

At scene boot the blocking "New Game" overlay asks the player to choose
Single-player vs Competitive **before** the tutorial offer is shown. A player
who actually wants the guided tutorial must therefore pick a game mode first,
even though the tutorial can only ever be played single-player — so the mode
choice is either wasted or misleading. The tutorial decision should be asked
first, and choosing the tutorial should commit the player to single-player
without an unnecessary mode choice.

## Users

- **First-time player (tutorial wanters).** "As a first-time player, I want to
  be asked whether I want the tutorial *before* I am asked to pick a mode, so
  that I am not forced to make a mode choice that the tutorial will ignore."
- **First-time player (tutorial decliners).** "As a first-time player who
  skips the tutorial, I want the Single-player/Competitive selector to appear
  immediately so I can start the game I actually want."
- **Returning player.** "As a returning player (tutorial already completed or
  skipped), I want the mode selector to appear straight away, unchanged from
  today."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. On boot, when the tutorial offer is eligible, the tutorial offer modal is
   presented **before** the New Game mode selector (Single-player vs
   Competitive); the mode selector is not visible while the tutorial offer is
   waiting.
2. Selecting **Start Tutorial** starts the existing scripted tutorial as a
   single-player game and the New Game mode selector is not shown for that
   boot. (The tutorial is only available in single-player.)
3. Selecting **Skip for now** on the tutorial offer presents the New Game
   mode selector next, and confirming it starts the selected mode exactly as
   today.
4. When the tutorial offer is **not** eligible (completed, already skipped,
   replay mode, or disabled), the New Game mode selector is presented as the
   first boot modal, exactly as today.
5. The deferred week banner still fires **exactly once** and only after the
   player has committed to playing (after mode confirmation, or suppressed
   for the tutorial path as today). It must not fire while any boot modal is
   waiting for a choice.
6. A browser smoke test asserts the modal ordering: tutorial offer visible
   first; after skipping, the mode selector is visible.
7. A unit test asserts the ordering decision in
   `showTutorialOfferOrDeferredBanner` (tutorial offer before mode selector,
   and the mode selector is skipped entirely when the tutorial is started).
8. The scene-restart / menu round-trip behaviour is preserved: the boot flow
   is presented once per boot, and re-presented after `scene.restart()` /
   `scene.start()` (regression guard).
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (for example
   the onboarding flow section of `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-5.md`).
10. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No changes to the tutorial script/steps, tutorial content, or competitive
  gameplay/state semantics.
- Reuse the existing `TutorialOfferModal` and `MainStreetNewGameOverlay`
  components and the existing localisation keys; no new user-facing strings
  are required unless the producer asks for an explicit "tutorial is
  single-player" note (see Assumptions).
- Must not regress the deferred-banner timing guarantees currently pinned by
  `tests/main-street/week-banner.browser.test.ts`.
- Must not regress the once-per-boot selector guard
  (`newGameSelectionMade` / `resetNewGameSelectionFlag`).

## Existing state

- `showTutorialOfferOrDeferredBanner` in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerTutorial.ts` currently shows
  `newGameOverlay` first and only calls `showTutorialOfferOnly` from the
  overlay's `onConfirm` callback.
- `TutorialOfferModal.onSkip` (wired in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts`) currently calls
  `s.playDeferredWeekBanner()` directly.
- `TutorialOfferModal.onStartTutorial` already builds a single-player
  tutorial state via `createTutorialScenario()` and starts the tutorial flow.
- `applyNewGameSelection` (in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.ts`) rebuilds state only for
  competitive; single-player keeps the existing state.
- Eligibility is decided by `shouldShowTutorialOffer` in
  `src/TutorialState.ts` (`not_seen` shows; `completed`/`skipped` do not;
  `forceShowOffer` overrides; `replayMode`/`disableTutorial` suppress).
- The current implementation order contradicts the onboarding flow documented
  in `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-5.md` §5 (tutorial check before normal
  run), which predates the competitive mode selector.

## Desired change

Reorder the boot flow so the tutorial offer is the **first** blocking modal:

1. If `showIfEligible` returns true → show the tutorial offer modal.
   - **Start Tutorial** → run the existing single-player tutorial; do not show
     the mode selector this boot.
   - **Skip for now** → show the New Game mode selector.
2. If the offer is ineligible → show the New Game mode selector.
3. After the mode selector is confirmed → `applyNewGameSelection` then play
   the deferred week banner (exactly once).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerTutorial.ts` — reorder
  `showTutorialOfferOrDeferredBanner` / `showTutorialOfferOnly` so the offer
  precedes the selector.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — rewire
  `onStartTutorial` / `onSkip` callbacks to the reordered flow; keep the
  tutorial single-player setup and the deferred-banner hand-off.
- `src/scenes/TutorialOfferModal.ts` — skip callback should no longer assume
  it owns the deferred-banner hand-off (if the reorder moves that
  responsibility).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetNewGameOverlay.ts` — only if the once-per-boot guard
  needs adjusting.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-new-game-restart.test.ts` — update ordering
  expectations for the selector guard.
- `tests/main-street/tutorial-offer-modal.test.ts` — add ordering/decision
  coverage where testable without Phaser.
- `tests/main-street/week-banner.browser.test.ts` — pin the deferred-banner
  timing under the new order.
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-5.md` — update the onboarding flow section
  to state that the tutorial offer precedes the mode selector.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUTU8INS009MRR1** — Game-mode selector UI (introduced the current
  boot-time selector ordering).
- **MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP** — Playable AI competitive mode (parent epic of the
  selector).
- Automated related-work report appended by `/skill:find-related`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — no copy change.** The modal body/buttons keep their current
  localised copy. The "tutorial is single-player" fact is enforced by the flow
  (choosing the tutorial skips the mode selector) rather than stated in the
  UI. If the producer wants the modal copy to say "single-player", that is an
  additive copy/CSV change.
- **Assumption — tutorial start implies single-player.** "Start Tutorial"
  never shows the mode selector, matching the constraint that the tutorial is
  single-player only.
- **Risk — deferred-banner timing.** Moving the skip hand-off must preserve
  "fires exactly once, never while a modal is waiting". Covered by AC5/AC6.
- **Risk — guard interplay.** The `newGameSelectionMade` once-per-boot guard
  must not suppress the selector when the tutorial offer is skipped, and must
  not show the selector after the tutorial is started.
- **Risk — stale browser tests.** `tests/**/*.browser.test.ts` are excluded
  from `npm run test` (unit project only), so browser-ordering tests must be
  run explicitly via the browser profile to verify AC6.
- **Scope creep.** Repositioning/replay of the tutorial from Settings and any
  "tutorial is single-player" copy change are out of scope unless requested;
  record as linked work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the New Game mode selector be skipped entirely when the player
  chooses Start Tutorial (i.e. the tutorial always runs single-player)?" —
  Answer (operator, seed instruction): "If the player wants to play the
  tutorial they can only play single player. Ask if they want the tutorial
  before asking if they want to play single or competitive." Source:
  `/intake` seed command.
- Q: "Should the tutorial offer modal copy explicitly state that the tutorial
  is single-player only?" — Answer: OPEN QUESTION (not specified in the seed).
  Assumption recorded: no copy change; enforced by flow. Research: modal copy
  is localised in `src/i18n/tutorial-en.csv` and covered by
  `tests/main-street/tutorial-i18n.test.ts` / `tutorial-csv.test.ts`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ** – Reroll to cost more (completed)
- **MS-0MUTU8J9T0034OT7** – Competitive scoreboard & active-seat HUD (completed)
- **MS-0MUVUPWHD0032CU4** – Turns do not bank when playing against AI (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ac5, acceptance, actually, add, additive (+229 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, actually, add, already, always (+176 more)
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: ac6, acceptance, actually, add, additive (+172 more)

## Goal

## Context

discovered-from:MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M. On the canonical `mc-balance` Medium profile (200 seeds, 60 turns, greedy), the branching level-0 prerequisites `upg-drive-in` (cost 700) and `upg-wellness-center` (cost 900) remain at/near 0% M1 because they compete for the single upgrade market slot with the standard path (`upg-imax`, `upg-resort-spa`) weighted by MS-0MUYK08I1004I19W. Raising their `drawWeight` lifted them but nudged the level-2 capstone `upg-luxury-retreat` below 5%, so MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M left them unchanged rather than over-tune the market.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Canonical before/after Monte Carlo evidence (200 seeds, `mc-balance`, 60 turns, greedy Easy/Medium/Hard) records M1 for `upg-drive-in` and `upg-wellness-center`.
2. A card-data-only change (cost/`incomeBonus`/`drawWeight`) lifts both to >=5% M1 on Medium without regressing the four level-2 capstones below 5% and without breaking the Easy >= Medium >= Hard win-rate ladder.
3. Full test suite passes.

## Constraints

Card data only; no engine-rule change. If unreachable, document the shortfall and escalate separately.

As a Main Street player, I want installed entitled packs' cards dealt into my game and restored on load, so new content is persistent and save-compatible.

Cross-repo child of Tableau-Card-Engine CG-0MUZIS410002Z8EH (epic CG-0MUZFD1WR0031QTB, DLC support for card packs). The core contract/loader/merge landed in the engine (F1-F7); this item is the Main Street consumer.

- A missing or disabled pack degrades gracefully: warn, continue with base content, and refuse only when a live card instance requires a missing template.

data.comment:
## Clarifying Questions

**Q1: Alternating turn structure for shared-street mode.** The description notes this is a design decision to confirm. Which approach do you prefer?

- **Option A — Alternating MarketPhases within a shared day:** Each day has one MarketPhase where players alternate turns (Player A acts, Player B acts, Player A acts, etc.), then shared Income/Incident/EndCheck phases resolve once both players have had a chance to act. This creates tight interplay — each player reacts to the other's placements before income/event resolution.
- **Option B — Alternating full days:** Each player gets their own full day/turn cycle (Player A's complete day: Market -> Income -> Incident -> EndCheck, then Player B's complete day). This is simpler to implement and closer to the existing single-player flow.

**Preference?** (Option A / Option B / Other approach)

data.author: Map
data.comment:
**Q2: Child item coverage.** The epic lists 5 ACs. AC1 (state model), AC2 (AI strategy), AC3 (income/events), and AC4 (Monte Carlo) map to existing/sub-plan children. AC5 (game scene) is noted as "may be split into a child at planning." Should we create the AC5 child now (competitive-mode scene with owner-coloured street, turn alternation, SLL layout, audio feedback), or defer to planning?

**Q3: Denial reasoning scope.** The AI-strategy child (CG-0MT5X3N79002S038) explicitly marks opponent-aware *denial* reasoning as out of scope. Confirm: denial (blocking opponent's best slot, buying to deny) is intentionally deferred to a follow-up? Or should we include basic denial as a minimum viable feature?

**Q4: Win condition for competitive mode.** The single-player win condition is a score threshold. In competitive mode, does the game end when:
- Either player reaches the threshold (first to win), or
- A fixed number of shared days elapses (higher score wins), or
- Both reach threshold / both go bankrupt (simultaneous end)?

**Preference?**

data.author: Map
data.comment:
## Producer Decisions (intake response)

**Q1: Alternating turn structure — Answer: Option A**
Alternating MarketPhases within a shared day. Each day has one MarketPhase where players alternate turns (Player A acts, Player B acts, etc.), then shared Income/Incident/EndCheck phases resolve once both have acted.

**Q2: Child item coverage for AC5 — Answer: Deferred to planning**
AC5 (competitive-mode scene) will be created as a child work item during planning. For now, focus on the engine/state layer (AC1-AC4).

**Q3: Denial reasoning scope — Answer: Deferred**
Opponent-aware denial reasoning (blocking the opponent's best slot, buying to deny) is intentionally deferred to a follow-up child.

**Q4: Win condition — Answer: First to threshold wins, with optional endless mode**
When either player reaches the win threshold, that player wins. The game includes an option to carry on in endless mode where both players continue building beyond the threshold.

**Clarification on "owner-coloured street" (AC5):** This means rendering the shared street grid where each business slot is visually tinted to show which player owns it — e.g., player businesses get a blue tint, AI opponent's businesses get a red tint. This is a visual UI concern for the scene child (deferred to planning).

| F7 | Full-suite and build verification `MS-0MUYGFXMK009L1UU` | task | F1–F5 |

## Acceptance-criteria coverage (parent → child)

- Parent AC1 (population reflects reputation) → F2 (pure helper), F4 (live count).
- Parent AC2 (wander the street, no gameplay RNG) → F3.
- Parent AC3 (live population update) → F4.
- Parent AC4 (income sourced from pedestrians; credited total unchanged) → F5, guarded by F1.
- Parent AC5 (reduced-motion/replay exemptions, non-blocking, no new RNG) → F1, F3, F4, F5.
- Parent AC6 (documentation updated) → F6.
- Parent AC7 (build and full suite green) → F7.

_Note:_ the parent ACs are a numbered list, so the automated coverage helper (`tree_coverage.run_coverage_review`) extracts zero parent ACs and returns `proceed` (100%). The mapping above is the human traceability record. Parent formatting was left unchanged to preserve author intent.

## Automated review stages

1. **Requirements & AC alignment** — every parent AC maps to ≥1 child AC (above); no invented requirements; out-of-scope items kept out of the children.
2. **Completeness** — every child has a description, `## Acceptance Criteria`, and `**Key Files:**`; key-file paths validated (each has a `/` and an extension); predicted parent paths corrected to the repo's actual layout (`src/scenes/...`, `src/coin-grid.ts`).
3. **Sequencing & dependencies** — test-first: F1 (invariant regression tests) precedes the phase rework (F5); edges F3←F2, F4←F3, F5←F3+F1, F6←F4+F5, F7←F1..F5.
4. **Scope sizing** — 7 deliverable increments; each is a minimal end-to-end slice (code + tests + docs).
5. **Acceptance & testability** — child ACs are pass/fail and testable (unit + browser tests, credited-total assertions, exemption tests).
6. **Polish & handoff** — child titles ≤7 words; descriptions copy-pasteable for `implement`.
7. **AC coverage review** — `recommendation: proceed`.

## Assumptions (documented)

- The layer is parented to the street container so it pans/clips with the street camera view.
- Presentation randomness is a module-local seeded PRNG, never the seeded gameplay RNG.
- Edge case: `repBonus` can be > 0 while zero pedestrians are on screen (repBonus is independent of the current reputation total). `dissolveIntoCoins` falls back to a street-area anchor (road band / street centre) — never the HUD counter. The producer may override this fallback.
- Per-seat competitive populations are out of scope until `MS-0MUXAQQON006XA6I` lands.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No new questions were required in this planning session. The intake Appendix (Q1–Q6) already answers appearance (solid silhouettes, `#88bbff`), wandering (free wander), ratio (1 per 50, uncapped), conversion (figures dissolve into coins; credited total unchanged), live vs end-of-turn (live fade in/out) and density cap (uncapped). No prior answer was changed or superseded.

Root cause (per audit CG-C0MUA8BY8B0073M4S): under concurrent full-suite Chromium contention (2 suites × 4 browser workers) the Phaser game loop is starved of animation frames. The drag began against a not-yet-registered hit zone (Phaser only flushes _pendingInsertion during InputPlugin.preUpdate on its rAF tick, never from a setTimeout), so the drop was silently missed and the transfer animation never started — the waitForCondition then timed out.

Fix in tests/main-street/upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts:
1. waitForFrames() (2 rAF callbacks) before the first mousedown in beginDrag, so the game loop registers freshly rebuilt drop zones + draggable containers before the gesture starts (pattern from expanded-viewport.browser.test.ts).
2. waitForCondition now polls on requestAnimationFrame instead of setTimeout(25), guaranteeing a full game-loop step (InputPlugin.preUpdate) per poll so the queued drop handler fires.
3. Transfer-animation wait budget widened to 30s.

Docs: docs/DEVELOPER.md browser-test mitigation conventions updated (rAF-before-gesture + rAF-polling for frame-gated waits).

Verification: upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts passes 6/6 across repeated runs; build green; implement.py finish full-suite gate passed; unit tests green for related suites.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
## Blocked — new AC is ambiguous and conflicts with the open parent item

**Question for the producer. I have not modified any code because the definition gate fails.**

### Context

The producer audit of 2026-09-21 rejected the previous attempt and requested:

> "We need a new AC in which no tutorial step proceeds without using the available action point."

This requirement is **not** in the work item's formal acceptance criteria, and it conflicts with the still-open parent item **CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P** ("Main Street: tutorial coverage for action banking"), whose AC1 requires the banking hint to fire **while the tutorial is active** when the player ends a turn with spare actions.

### Current code state (dev)

The prior one-line fix (commit `8ffdae34`, branch `fix-bank-hint-tutorial`, author Sorra the Orc) is **not merged into `dev`**. On `dev` the original condition is still present at `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts:118`:

```ts
if (tut?.isActive && s.state.actionsRemaining > 0) {
```

### Why the requested AC needs clarification

A literal reading — block **End Turn** during the tutorial while `actionsRemaining > 0`, forcing the player to spend the action point first — **deadlocks the 26-step flow**:

- Day 5 is **T15 Community Favour** then **T16 End Turn**.
- T15 is a *free* once-per-turn action and does **not** consume the daily action (`TutorialFlow.ts` and `tests/main-street/tutorial-action-economy.test.ts` both assert this).
- The player therefore reaches T16 with 1 action remaining, and `isTutorialActionAllowed` only permits the current step's required action, so there is no legal way to spend it.

The scripted economy also intentionally leaves a spare action on several later days because of banking (see the "simulated run with banking" test).

### Questions

1. **Which behaviour is intended?**
   - **A. Block End Turn during the tutorial while actions remain** ("use your action point first" feedback). If so, how should Day 5 (T15 free Community Favour) be resolved — make T15 consume the daily action, restructure the T14/T16 day boundaries, or allow an extra spend during an end-turn step?
   - **B. Do not bank spare actions during the tutorial** (forfeit them) so the day budget never drifts, while End Turn stays allowed. Note this conflicts with parent AC1.
   - **C. Keep the one-line hint fix and add an assertion-only AC** that every action-gated step consumes exactly one action point, with no runtime change to End Turn.
   - **D. Other** — please give the exact AC wording and the expected player-visible behaviour.

2. Does parent item **CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P** still stand with AC1 as written, or should its AC1 be re-scoped/replaced by this item?

3. If the two items genuinely conflict, which item owns the fix?

Answering Q1 (and Q2) is sufficient for me to implement the hint fix plus the new AC with tests and push to `dev`.

### AC status

- AC1 (hint must not fire during tutorial): **unmet on `dev`** — the one-line fix exists only on the unmerged branch.
- AC2–AC5: **not yet verified** on `dev`.

data.comment:
## Intake: context gathered and open questions

### Context (from repo + work-item search)

- This work item is a migrated producer note: "Charity shop, 1.5 income per turn, 0.15 reputation per turn. Costs 3".
- Main Street uses a **×100 integer economy** (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6), so the note converts to: `cost = 300`, `baseIncome = 150`, `reputationPerTurn = 15`.
- Every business also pays a standard **ongoing cost** of one quarter of its purchase price (`75` for a 300-cost card, CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE), stored in the CSV `ongoingCost` column.
- Card rows live in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` and are the source of truth; `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` documents them. A new business generally also needs a catalog entry, tier registration (automatic via the CSV `tier` column), and tests.
- There is currently **no** charity shop (or equivalent thrift/op-shop) card in the CSV or catalog, so this is a net-new business template.
- Related work items:
  - `CG-0MUAYBA0L000XLK3` — Pawn shop should reduce, not increase reputation (sibling migrated note; sets the precedent for ×100 values and negative reputation).
  - `CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6` — integer economy (coin/rep ×100).
  - `CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE` — business ongoing cost (1/4 purchase price).
  - `CG-0MUIH30NQ0047W1I` — Reconcile event card text to integer data; `CG-0MTW1EN0D003CSA0` — validate all card text (ongoing text/data consistency).

### Open questions

**Q1 — Are the stated numbers gross or net of the standard ongoing cost?**
Every business pays `ongoingCost = cost / 4` per turn (`75` for a 300-cost card). "1.5 income per turn" is therefore ambiguous.

- **A (Recommended):** 1.5 is **gross `baseIncome`** → `baseIncome = 150`, `ongoingCost = 75`, net `0.75`/turn. Matches how every other business stat is documented (gross income + separate ongoing cost).
- **B:** 1.5 is **net after ongoing cost** → `baseIncome = 225`, `ongoingCost = 75`.
- **C:** The charity shop is **exempt from ongoing cost** → `baseIncome = 150`, `ongoingCost = 0`.

**Q2 — Which synergy type should the Charity Shop belong to?**
The CSV requires a `synergyTypes` value (affects adjacency bonuses).

- **A (Recommended):** `Commerce` — a charity shop retails donated second-hand goods (matches Pawn Shop / Boutique).
- **B:** `Service` — treated as a non-profit community service.
- **C:** `Culture` — a community/volunteering asset.
- **D:** No synergy (like Pawn Shop: `synergyCoinBonus = 0`, `synergyRepBonus = 0`).

**Q3 — Which progression tier, and should it have an upgrade path?**

- **A (Recommended):** `tier = 2`, standalone (`upgradePath = Charity Shop`, `maxLevel = 1`) — matches the other 300-cost, no-upgrade Commerce singles (Pawn Shop, Boutique).
- **B:** `tier = 1`, standalone (matches the 300-cost T1 basics: Bakery, Diner, Bookshop, Hardware Store).
- **C:** `tier = 2` with a single upgrade step (a new upgrade card name would be needed, e.g. "Charity Superstore").

### Non-blocking assumptions (will be used unless corrected)

- `family = business`, `id = biz-charity-shop`, `name = Charity Shop`.
- Description and `art_notes` generated in the existing house style (e.g. "Sells donated goods. … Provides +0.15 reputation per turn.").

(reject) → `evt-tax-inquiry` forms a cycle. The epic requires "sinks and
cycles are intentional" and a validator that fails loudly on dangling/unknown
references, plus a continuity indicator "including cycles".

- (A) **Cycles are a first-class supported shape**: validator reports them as
  informational, the graph/manifest marks cycle edges, the continuity
  indicator keeps showing while a cycle is live, and a test pins the shipped
  tax cycle. Content may add more cycles later.
- (B) Cycles allowed only when a CSV opt-in flag (e.g. `storylineCycle=allow`)
  is set; otherwise the validator fails. More guarding, one more CSV column.
- (C) Treat every cycle as an authoring error: fail validation, and re-cut the
  tax chain into an acyclic form (changes shipped content).

**Recommended:** (A) — the epic explicitly designs for recurring threads and
cycles; (C) contradicts the epic, and (B) adds a column before authoring pain
is demonstrated.

### Q7 — Deployment target of the tooling (blocks the validator slicing)

Epic constraint: "No new runtime dependency beyond the existing
Node/Vitest/scripts toolchain". Which implementation is expected for
`scripts/validate-storylines.ts` and the graph export, given the sibling has
no `scripts/` dir today (only `src/scripts/`, run via `tsx`/`vite-node`)?

- (A) **Node-runnable TypeScript in the sibling's `src/scripts/` (or a new
  `scripts/`) executed with the existing `tsx` devDependency**, wired as
  `validate:storylines` in `package.json` and invoked by a Vitest test and a
  pre-push hook — no new dependency.
- (B) A Vitest-only test-module validator (no standalone CLI), so the check
  rides the existing suite and no npm script/hook is added.
- (C) A standalone `.mjs` Node script with no TypeScript compilation step.

**Recommended:** (A) — it satisfies "non-zero exit on failure" and
"wired into the test suite / pre-push" literally and reuses the existing
`tsx`/`vite-node` toolchain, where (B) cannot be run as a standalone gate and
(C) duplicates CSV parsing outside the typed model.

### Q8 — Pre-push hook: which repo, and is it opt-in?

AC4/AC10 say validation is "enforced in the test suite or pre-push hook". The
core repo is the one with the shared hook setup; the CSV lives in the sibling.

- (A) **Enforce in the sibling's Vitest suite** (unit-failure on invalid
  storylines) **and** add an opt-in `pre-push` reminder in the sibling; no
  hook change in the core repo.
- (B) Enforce only via the sibling unit suite (no hook).
- (C) Add a mandatory pre-push hook in both repos that runs the validator.

**Recommended:** (A) — the suite gate satisfies the AC, and an opt-in hook
gives local feedback without making every core-repo push depend on the
sibling checkout being present.

## Fix summary — upgrade-drag-drop browser contention flake

Root cause (two interacting mechanisms, both environmental under full-suite load):

1. **rAF starvation.** Phaser only flushes newly created interactive hit zones (`_pendingInsertion` → `_list`) during `InputPlugin.preUpdate`, which runs on the game-loop tick. The tick is driven by `requestAnimationFrame`; under heavy concurrent-suite contention rAF is starved, so the synthetic drag gesture was dispatched against a not-yet-registered hit zone and never engaged.
2. **Late market rebuild.** The async SVG prewarm chain (`cardSvgLoadPromise.then(prewarm).then(refreshAll)`) rebuilds the market containers after the SVGs load. Under contention that rebuild landed after the test captured a container, so the gesture dragged a detached object.

Changes (commit chain on dev):
- `39894ee4` — raise `beginDrag` retry deadline 15s → 30s.
- `7d316b9e` — deterministic teardown: new shared helper `tests/helpers/phaserCanvasPool.ts` runs the deferred `runDestroy()` synchronously and drains Phaser's CanvasPool; used by `upgrade-drag-drop` and `market-deal-in`.
- `45988451` — step the game loop directly with `TimeStep.step(time)` (`stepGame`) instead of awaiting rAF; `market-deal-in` re-resolves the last market call while stepping.
- `2279dbc3` — `beginDrag` takes the scene explicitly and accepts a `resolve` callback that re-finds the live container each attempt (returns the container actually dragged); `waitForMarketStable` awaits `cardSvgLoadPromise` and requires sustained stability. Also raised the browser-stage wall-clock bound in `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` 15 → 20 min (115 files now run ~13-15 min nominal, so variance straddled the old bound) and updated `docs/DEVELOPER.md`.

## Validation evidence
- **A/B under simulated rAF starvation** (temporary 5s rAF throttle): old rAF-based version **failed** (60s timeout); new `stepGame` version **passed** in 2s.
- **Forced mid-gesture rebuild** (`scene.refreshAll()` before the drag, asserting the container identity changed): `resolve` still engages the drag.
- **Full browser stage**: 115 files / 664 tests green (multiple runs).
- **Full suite** (`npm test`, unit + browser + tutorial E2E): green at `2279dbc3`.

## Notes / residual risk

data.author: Map
data.comment:
## Clarifying Questions (Round 2 — follow-up from codebase research)

Thanks for the answers. Researching the code surfaced three more decisions I cannot resolve from the repo alone. **Recommended** options are advisory only.

**Q5: Persistent Steam achievement?**
The codebase maps *all 12* existing challenges 1:1 to persistent Steam achievements (`src/MainStreetAchievements.ts` → `CHALLENGE_TO_ACHIEVEMENT_ID`, enforced by `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` against the launcher manifest `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json`, which lives in the **`core` git submodule — a separate repository**).
- (a) Map it to a persistent Steam achievement, consistent with the other 12. Requires: a `core`-submodule manifest entry + a new Steamworks backend API name (producer/external action), plus the `MainStreetAchievements.ts` mapping. These cross-repo pieces can be split into a blocking child work item so this item stays run-local.
- (b) Run-local challenge only (no Steam achievement) — requires relaxing the achievement completeness/drift tests that currently assert one achievement per challenge.
- (c) Other (specify).

**Recommended:** (a) — keeps the challenge system consistent; the `core`/Steamworks pieces become a separate blocking child item.

**Q6: Which sale actions count toward the 3?**
- (a) Only street/tableau sales via the **Manage Card → Sell** dialog (the interactive path). This is tracked by the existing `soldSlots` array, is cumulative and undo-aware, and needs no new state. Note: sold cards cannot be closed, so the count only ever rises.
- (b) Every business sale, including from hand (`sellFromHand`) and the legacy `sellFromTableau` path (used by tests) — requires adding a new cumulative counter to game state, plus save/load + undo plumbing.
- (c) Other (specify).

**Recommended:** (a) — the challenge reads as a street/economy goal, and `soldSlots` already persists cumulatively and is restored correctly on undo.

**Q7: Player-facing title** (and thus the achievement name). Existing style is terse ("Renovator", "Deep Pockets", "Bustling Street"):
- (a) "Serial Seller"
- (b) "Wheel and Deal"
- (c) "Turning a Profit"
- (d) Other (specify).

**Recommended:** (a) "Serial Seller" — clearly conveys selling multiple businesses and matches the terse title style.

Proposed description (Q7 follow-on, confirm or amend): *"Sell 3 or more businesses in a single game."*

Once these are answered I can draft and finish the intake brief. I will proceed automatically from any unanswered minor items using the recommended option, documented as an assumption.

### What changed
- `src/MainStreetChallenges.ts`: added the `economic` category, an optional `progress?: (state) => { current, target }` provider on `Challenge`, the `ch-serial-seller` template (title **Serial Seller**, description "Sell 3 or more businesses in a single game.", evaluator counts `state.soldSlots`, target 3), and the pure `formatChallengeProgress()` helper. - `challenges.test.ts`: 13-template count, Serial Seller evaluator (empty/1/2/3 sold), selection inclusion, progress metadata + `formatChallengeProgress`, no-progress on the other 12.

Adding the 13th template shifts the seeded Fisher-Yates challenge shuffle, which shifts the per-run RNG stream and therefore deterministic replay outcomes. `competitive-monte-carlo.test.ts` seed `'ac1-cap-1'` now ends via `reputation_collapse` before the 5-turn cap; updated that one assertion to seed `'ac1-cap-3'`, which still exercises `max_turns_cap`. data.comment:
question: **Producer decisions needed before intake can complete — IT Specialist and Delivery Driver mechanics.**

The two cards' advertised cost reductions have no implementing mechanic and their stated target ("this business") cannot be resolved as written (the market refresh is a single global re-roll; the employing slot is already occupied). `CG-0MTKMGL66004I0PC` deferred this as Q4. Three decisions are blocking:

**Q1 — IT Specialist ("Reduces this business refresh cost by 100").** There is no per-business refresh; `refreshMarketCost` is a single global re-roll (`REFRESH_MARKET_COST = 500`) already reduced street-wide by the Accountant's `refreshCostDiscount` and the Negotiator skill (−100).
- (a) Reuse `refreshCostDiscount = 100` on `staff-it` (street-wide; stacks with Accountant/Negotiator) and reword the description to remove "this business".
- (b) Introduce a new per-business "refresh" mechanic scoped to the employing business (new action/engine concept).
- (c) Other (describe).
**Recommended:** (a) — reuses an already-wired mechanic, adds zero engine surface, and matches the Accountant/Negotiator precedent.

**Q2 — Delivery Driver ("Reduces business card purchase cost by 50 for this business").** No purchase-cost-discount field exists; `purchaseBusiness` (click) and `buyAndPlaceBusiness` (drag, +50% premium) charge `card.cost` directly.
- (a) Add `purchaseCostDiscount = 50` and apply it street-wide to business/community-space purchases (click and drag; discount base before premium) while employed; reword the description.
- (b) Scope the discount to placements in slots adjacent to the driver's employing business (new adjacency mechanic).
- (c) Leave unimplemented and remove/reword the description so no unimplemented claim remains.
- (d) Other (describe).
**Recommended:** (a) — smallest new surface, mirrors the established discount-then-premium rule, and gives the card a real effect.

**Q3 — Description/catalog/guard and CSV-schema handling.** If (a) is chosen for either card, the CSV description and catalog "Ability" cell change from per-business to street-wide, the regression guard contracts get a real `column`, and a new `purchaseCostDiscount` column must be added to `src/card-data.csv`, parsed into `StaffCard`, and coordinated with core `src/balance-cards/csv.ts` + the `./core` submodule pin (precedent `MS-0MULW540X009EP9A`).
- (a) Yes — reword to street-wide, back both descriptions with data columns, and coordinate the new column across game + core.
- (b) Keep the current "this business" wording even if the implemented scope is street-wide (accept a text/mechanic mismatch).
- (c) Other (describe).
**Recommended:** (a) — the item's goal is for each description to be backed by a data column; a mismatch would reopen the gap this item closes.

Note: `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ` (Reroll to cost more) also changes `refreshMarketCost` semantics; confirm ordering if both land together. Full brief and Appendix are in the work-item description.

data.comment:
## C2 implementation complete — storyline model & extraction seam

### Delivered

**Types** (`src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`): optional `storylineId`/`storylineTitle` on `EventCard`; new `StorylineOption` (`label`, `successorId`, `effectPolicy: 'apply'|'skip'`) and `CompiledStoryline` types.

**Extraction seam** (`src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`, new): game-agnostic pure functions — `compileStorylineFromEvent`, `getStorylineOptions`, `registerStorylineOptions`/`resetStorylineRegistry`, `eventHasStoryline`, `storylineOptionCount`, `resolveStorylineOption`, `createPendingStorylineChoice`, `markChoiceResolved`, `recordStorylineResolution`, `pushChainCard` (moved out of the engine to break a module cycle).

**Engine** (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`): new generalised `resolveEventOption(state, optionIndex)` API; `resolveEventChoice('accept'|'reject')` is now a thin backward-compatible wrapper (index 0/1). Legacy two-option cards record the lowercase `accept`/`reject` token so the transcript and pending-state shape are unchanged.

**Parser** (`src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts`): parses the two new CSV columns.

**CSV** (`src/card-data.csv`): two columns appended (`storylineId`, `storylineTitle`); all pre-existing columns are byte-for-byte semantically unchanged (verified by diffing the first 43 columns of every row — 0 content differences). 11 shipped cards assigned to 5 named storylines. `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` refreshed to match.

**State** (`src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`, `MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`): `PendingEventChoice.chosenOption` generalised to `string | null`; save/load unchanged and legacy-compatible. `EventChoiceResolution.option` generalised to `string`.

### CSA semantics decision (important)

A bare `storylineId` is **descriptive metadata only** (grouping/journal) and does **not** make a card a choice. Only `hasChoices` or a registered option list intercepts resolution. Terminal escalation cards (`evt-depression`, `evt-pandemic`, `evt-general-strike`, `evt-farm-table`) carry a `storylineId` for grouping but still resolve as plain incidents. This was caught by the Monte Carlo balance guardrail: an initial over-broad `eventHasStoryline` (storylineId ⇒ choice) raised the MC win rate 0.85 → 1.00; the corrected semantics restore 0.85. Two tests pin this.

### Migration notes (handoff to C6)

- The compiled option list is a **linear ordered sequence**; resolution selects one option by index. No branching graph traversal.
- `compileStorylineFromEvent` is the sole compilation entry point; `resolveStorylineOption` applies the effect policy and returns the successor id; the caller pushes it.
- Callers never reach into Main-Street-only resolution internals: everything goes through `MainStreetStoryline`.
- `resolveEventOption` is the generalised public API; legacy `resolveEventChoice` delegates to it.
- Portable to the core engine: the seam depends only on a state shape and a template registry supplied by the caller.

### Tests

- New `tests/main-street/storyline-model.test.ts` — 34 tests covering AC1 (metadata + parser), AC2 (compilation, legacy-equivalence, multi-option, out-of-range, double-resolve), AC3 (purity, defensive copies, seam API, `pushChainCard` determinism, effect policies).
- C1 regression harness (56 tests) and all pre-existing storyline tests remain green.
- Full suite: 249 files / 4119 passed (3 skipped) via the test-skill runner.

- **`package.json`** — `validate:storylines` script, run via `vite-node` (required because the model imports `card-data.csv?raw`; plain `tsx` cannot resolve the query suffix — same constraint as `monte-carlo`/`save-load-smoke`).
- **`src/scripts/install-storylines-pre-push.sh`** — opt-in, **non-blocking** local pre-push reminder installer (`--remove` supported). Never installed automatically; never blocks a push; local to the checkout (`.git/hooks`), so unrelated clones/CI are unaffected and the framework-managed `.githooks/` is untouched.
- **`tests/main-street/validate-storylines.test.ts`** — 31 tests.

### AC evidence

1. CLI exits 0 for the shipped CSV, non-zero for dangling-link / duplicate-id fixtures, naming the offending card and link. ✔ (subprocess tests)
2. Validation consumes the typed model (`getEventTemplates()` / `loadTemplatesFromCsv()`), not a hand-rolled CSV parse. ✔
3. Valid fixture plus at least one broken fixture per failure class. ✔
4. The shipped tax cycle is informational (exit 0, reported as `[cycle]`); an unintentional cycle is surfaced the same way; `--fail-on-cycle` turns it into a hard error. ✔
5. Suite gate: in-process test asserts `validateStorylines(getEventTemplates())` has zero issues, so the unit project fails if the shipped storylines break. ✔
6. Opt-in pre-push reminder documented and tested (install/idempotency/remove; non-blocking). ✔
7. Full suite green via the test-skill runner. ✔

### Cycle policy note

The shipped tax cycle (`evt-tax → evt-tax-inquiry → evt-tax-error → evt-tax`) is reported as a first-class informational finding. The validator prints `RESULT: VALID` and exits 0, consistent with the producer decision that cycles are intentional.

### Docs hand-off to C6

The validator is the documented one-command gate: `npm run validate:storylines` (options: `--json`, `--csv <path>`, `--fail-on-cycle`). C6 should document the command, the failure classes and the opt-in `install-storylines-pre-push.sh` reminder in the canonical storyline docs.

## Implementation notes (Map)

### What changed
- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — added `StorylineEventRecord` and an optional `storylineEvents` field on `MonteCarloRunSummary`; extracted the shared per-seed loop into `simulateSeed`; wraps each run in a temporary `MainStreetTranscriptRecorder` (restoring the previous recorder afterwards) so the engine's `event-choice` events are captured, then derives enriched records (storyline id + 1-based chain depth + successor) via `deriveStorylineEvents`.
- `src/MainStreetTranscript.ts` — additive `getMainStreetRecorder()` getter (needed to save/restore the recorder; no behaviour change).
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/storyline-metrics.ts` (new) — S1–S4 analytics (fire frequency, chain depth, cycle stats, choice win-rate delta) with graceful `null` degradation.
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/index.ts` — barrel exports.
- `docs/main-street/balance-analysis-api.md` — S1–S4 API reference section.
- `tests/main-street/balance/storyline-metrics.test.ts` (new) — 20 tests (unit + harness integration).

### Key decisions / assumptions
1. **Chain depth (AC2)** — defined as the 1-based position of an event within its successor chain (root = 1); a chain continues when an event's base ID equals the successor queued by the previous event of the same storyline, otherwise a fresh chain starts at depth 1. `computeChainDepthStats` reports mean/median/max over the per-event depth distribution grouped by storyline. The plan comment explicitly left this to the implementer.
2. **Cycle detection (AC3)** — a cycle occurrence is a chain transition that revisits a base event ID already seen in the current chain (the shipped tax loop). This is derived purely from the recorded sequence (`successorId` links), so `computeCycleStats` is self-contained and testable.
3. **Choice delta (AC4)** — a run is classified by its **first** recorded choice for the event (a run may revisit an event in a cycle); `value = winRateWhenAccept − winRateWhenReject`, mirroring M2.
4. **Graceful degradation (AC5)** — all four functions return `null` when no run summary carries a `storylineEvents` field; a present-but-empty array yields zeroed results (meaningful: no storylines fired).
5. **Recorder capture** — switched from the lazy `require('./MainStreetTranscript')` pattern to a static import for the recorder setup only. The lazy require silently no-ops under Vitest (and therefore captured nothing), while the existing `ai-action` require path is left untouched. `MainStreetTranscript` has no dependency back on the harness, so no cycle is introduced.
6. **Scope** — no CLI/UI wiring (per the Desired Change); the analytics are library functions consumed by the balance engine. CSV output is unchanged; JSON run summaries gain the `storylineEvents` field (the requested change).

### Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Changed/full unit suite via the test-skill runner: green (~38s).

# Intake Brief: Render the storyline graph (Mermaid to SVG) in the docs build (MS-0MUNB54KU005084C)

**Priority: Medium** | **Type: Chore** | **Assignee: Map**

> Discovered from the "write storylines" epic (`MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV`), C6
> documentation roadmap. The epic commits a generated Mermaid flowchart at
> `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd`; this item renders it to an image so
> the graph is viewable without a Mermaid-aware renderer and links it from the
> canonical storyline doc.

## Problem statement

The storyline graph is committed only as a Mermaid source file
(`docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd`). Anyone reading the repository on a
plain Markdown viewer, on GitHub without Mermaid support, or in a rendered docs
artefact cannot see the graph and cannot easily tell the shape of the shipped
storylines. Rendering it to a portable image (SVG, or PNG) in the docs build and
linking it from `docs/main-street/storylines.md` makes the graph viewable
everywhere, without requiring a Mermaid-aware renderer.

## Users

- **Content designers / producers** — need to see the storyline shape at a
  glance in the docs, without installing Mermaid tooling.
  - *"As a content designer, I want the storyline graph shown as an image in the
    docs, so I can inspect the shipped chains without a Mermaid renderer."*
- **Developers / reviewers** — need the rendered graph to stay in sync with the
  committed Mermaid source so reviews trust the picture.
  - *"As a reviewer, I want a drift guard between the rendered image and the
    committed `.mmd`, so a stale graph cannot be merged."*
- **Docs build / maintainers** — need a deterministic, reproducible render step
  with no manual copy-paste.
  - *"As a maintainer, I want one documented command that regenerates the
    rendered graph, so the artefact is reproducible."*

## Acceptance Criteria

> **Provisional — pending producer answers to Q1–Q3 below.** The ACs below
> assume the recommended options (new npm render script; reuse Playwright;
> SVG-vs-`.mmd` drift guard). They will be finalised once the open questions
> are answered.

1. **Rendered artefact** — a rendered graph image (SVG preferred; PNG
   acceptable) is committed under `docs/main-street/` and is viewable without a
   Mermaid-aware renderer.
2. **Reproducible render step** — a documented command (e.g. an npm script)
   renders the committed `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` into the image
   deterministically (no RNG, timestamp or wall-clock input; byte-identical on
   re-run).
3. **Doc link** — `docs/main-street/storylines.md` embeds or links the rendered
   image (replacing or complementing the current `.mmd` link in §11 Related
   documents).
4. **Drift guard (validation)** — an automated test/check fails when the
   committed rendered image drifts from the committed `.mmd`; optionally the
   check also fails when the `.mmd` drifts from `src/card-data.csv` (the
   `storylines:graph --check` CLI already supports this).
5. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No mandatory new runtime dependency for the game** — the existing epic
  constraint ("no new runtime dependency beyond the existing Node/Vitest/scripts
  toolchain for the tooling") should be respected where practical. Any renderer
  dependency is a **devDependency** only and must not enter the game bundle.
- **Determinism** — the render must be reproducible from the committed `.mmd`;
  no timestamps embedded in the output that would churn on every run.
- **Mermaid is the source of truth** — the `.mmd` remains the generated
  artefact of record; the image is derived, never hand-edited.
- **Licensing** — any added dependency must be permissively licensed (MIT,
  Apache-2.0, CC0).
- **Scope** — do not redesign the graph content or the storyline model; this
  item only renders and links the existing graph.

## Existing state (repo research)

- `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` — committed 98-line Mermaid flowchart;
  choice cards as diamonds, plain incidents as rounded rectangles, cycle edges
  as `==>`.
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` — generator/CLI: `--format mermaid|json`,
  `--out`, `--check` (drift guard). Deterministic (sorted ids, no RNG/clock).
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph-cli.ts` — CLI entry; npm script
  `storylines:graph` (`vite-node src/scripts/storyline-graph-cli.ts`).
- `tests/main-street/storyline-graph.test.ts` — asserts the committed `.mmd`
  matches regeneration from `src/card-data.csv` (existing drift guard).
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — canonical doc. §5 Tooling, §7.2 shipped
  graph, §10 Roadmap (links this work item), §11 Related documents (links the
  `.mmd`).
- `package.json` — scripts include `storylines:graph`, `validate:storylines`;
  devDependencies already include `playwright`, `sharp`, `vite-node`/`vite`,
  `vitest`. **No `mermaid`, `@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli`, `puppeteer` or docs site
  generator (mkdocs/docusaurus) is present anywhere in the repo or `core/`.**
- **There is no "docs build"** in `tce-main-street`: `docs/` is plain Markdown,
  there is no docs npm script, no mkdocs/docusaurus config, and no docs-site CI
  workflow. The only Pages workflow (`core/.github/workflows/deploy.yml`)
  deploys the game bundle, not these docs.

## Desired change

1. **Render** the committed `.mmd` into a portable image (SVG preferred) via a
   documented, deterministic script/npm command.
2. **Commit** the rendered image under `docs/main-street/`.
3. **Link/embed** the rendered image from `docs/main-street/storylines.md`.
4. **Guard** the rendered image against drift from the `.mmd` with a test/check,
   and document the regeneration workflow in the tooling table.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.svg` — **new** rendered artefact (or `.png`).
- `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` — input (unchanged source of truth).
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — add image embed/link; update §5 tooling.
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` — possibly extend with an `svg`/render format
  or a separate renderer module.
- `src/scripts/render-storyline-graph.ts` — **new** render script (if separate).
- `package.json` — new npm script (e.g. `storylines:graph:svg` or `docs:graph`).
- `tests/main-street/storyline-graph.test.ts` (or a new test) — rendered-image
  drift guard.
- Dev tooling only (if required) — a Mermaid renderer (see Q2).

## Related work

- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** — "write storylines" epic (completed/in review); this
  item is roadmap item C6-deferred.
- **MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0** — "Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema"
  (completed) — produced `storyline-graph.mmd`, the JSON manifest, and the
  existing `.mmd` drift test this item builds on.
- **MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY** — "Canonical docs, cross-references & doc-drift
  guard" (completed) — owns `docs/main-street/storylines.md` §10 Roadmap and §11
  Related documents.
- **MS-0MUNC8AOL0092BE5** — "Fix stale example-games/main-street paths in docs
  after the src/ migration" (open) — touches the same docs tree; coordinate if
  both touch `storylines.md`.
- **MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9** / **MS-0MUNB5D7K001GH19** — sibling deferred
  storyline roadmap items (conditional options; visual authoring editor).

### Related work (automated report)

- **MS-0MULWEEE8007J2TB** – Fix Accountant refreshCostDiscount value to ×100 scale (completed)
- **MS-0MTIILU5V006GCN4** – Competitive endless continuation (beyond win threshold) (open)
- **MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7** – Serial Seller: achievement manifest entry + Steamworks API name (completed)

## Risks & assumptions

- **No docs build exists (HIGH).** The premise "in the docs build" has no
  counterpart in the repo. *Mitigation:* Q1 decides whether to create a minimal
  render step, a full static docs build, or commit the image with no pipeline.
- **Renderer dependency tension (MEDIUM).** Rendering Mermaid needs a renderer
  (typically a headless Chromium). Adding a heavy dependency conflicts with the
  epic's "no new runtime dependency" constraint and adds CI weight.
  *Mitigation:* Q2 prefers reusing the already-installed Playwright Chromium;
  keep it dev-only.
- **Determinism / review churn (MEDIUM).** SVG output can embed ids/timestamps.
  *Mitigation:* assert byte-stable output in a test; pin renderer version.
- **Drift staleness (LOW).** A committed image can silently diverge from the
  `.mmd`. *Mitigation:* AC4 drift guard.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Requests to redesign the graph layout, add legends, or
  build a full docs site should be recorded as separate work items, not absorbed
  here.
- **Assumption** — SVG is the preferred format (scalable, text-searchable,
  no rasterisation dependency); PNG is acceptable only if the chosen renderer
  cannot emit SVG.
- **Assumption** — the `.mmd` stays the generated source of truth; the image is
  derived.
- **Assumption** — CHANGELOG is managed by the release pipeline and is out of
  scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

> **Status: producer input required.** The answers below are OPEN QUESTIONS.
> Recommendations are advisory only. On answer, the corresponding ACs and the
> Desired change will be finalised and the intake advanced to `intake_complete`.

- **Q1 — Delivery surface ("the docs build").** *There is no docs build in
  `tce-main-street` (docs are plain Markdown; no mkdocs/docusaurus/Pages
  pipeline). How should the rendered graph be delivered?*
  Options:
  - **(A) Add a minimal render step** — a new npm script (e.g.
    `storylines:graph:svg` or `docs:graph`) that renders `storyline-graph.mmd`
    → `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.svg`, with the SVG committed and
    regenerated like the `.mmd`.
  - **(B) Create a full static docs build** (mkdocs/docusaurus/Pages) that
    renders Mermaid at build time — larger scope, new toolchain.
  - **(C) Commit a one-off rendered SVG** with no build/pipeline; document
    manual regeneration only.
  - **Recommended: (A)** — smallest change that makes the graph viewable
    everywhere and keeps it reproducible, without adopting a docs-site
    toolchain the repo does not otherwise use.
  - **Answer:** OPEN QUESTION.

- **Q2 — Renderer / dependency policy.** *Rendering Mermaid requires a renderer;
  none is installed, and the epic constrained new runtime deps. Which renderer?*
  Options:
  - **(A) Add `@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli` (`mmdc`) as a devDependency** —
    bundles a Puppeteer/Chromium download; heaviest.
  - **(B) Reuse the already-installed `playwright` Chromium** and add the
    `mermaid` JS package as a devDependency, rendering headlessly.
  - **(C) No build-time renderer** — author/commit the SVG manually; guard
    drift only lightly.
  - **Recommended: (B)** — Playwright is already a devDependency (no second
    Chromium download) and keeps the renderer dev-only; the `mermaid` package
    is permissively licensed (MIT).
  - **Answer:** OPEN QUESTION.

- **Q3 — Drift gate scope.** *The item says "optionally fail the docs build when
  the committed `.mmd` drifts … (the CLI already supports `--check`)". Should
  the new step also fail when the rendered SVG drifts from the `.mmd`?*
  Options:
  - **(A) Yes** — add an SVG-vs-`.mmd` drift guard (test/script), in addition
    to the existing `.mmd`-vs-CSV guard. [Recommended]
  - **(B) No** — render the SVG but do not gate on it.
  - **Recommended: (A)** — a stale rendered graph is exactly the failure this
    item is meant to prevent.
  - **Answer:** OPEN QUESTION.
